newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Nordbanken posts Q1 profit fall.
newsitem.headline: Nordbanken posts Q1 profit fall.

text.p: Swedish bank Nordbanken posted a 10 percent fall in operating profit to 1.40 billion crowns ($179.4 million) on Tuesday, citing rising market interest rates that caused its bond portfolio to swing into deficit.
The profit was lower than the 1.70 billion crowns analysts in a Reuter poll had forecast, but the share still leapt on the Stockholm Stock Exchange.
At 1240 GMT, the share was up 3.8 percent, or nine crowns, at 243 crowns, while the bourse's general index was 1.21 percent higher at 2,609.03.
Analaysts did not think the report had affected the share much, saying it was more likely that it was once again riding on merger speculation.
"It's possible that the share is benefitting from renewed speculation about a merger between Nordbanken and S-E-Banken," a trader said.
The banks broke off merger talks earlier this year but analysts expect them to go through with a merger eventually.

Nordbanken's bond portfolio swung to a deficit with the net result from financial operations plunging to a charge of 128 million crowns from a credit of 245 million crowns in the first quarter of 1996, the bank said in its earnings statement.
"The rising market interest rates during the first quarter affected the holdings of financial current assets adversely," it said.

Nordbanken's net interest income fell four percent to 2.49 billion crowns, hurt by the charge for the government's deposit guarantee, which more than doubled to 110 million crowns, and a five billion crown share redemption in October 1996.

"Moreover, development was affected by declining interest margins, particularly on deposits, which could not be fully offset by rising deposit and lending volumes," the bank said, without giving any figures.
Lending to the corporate and public sectors, which rose sharply twoard the end of 1996, continued to rise but at a more moderate rate, it said.
"Lending to the private sector also rose through the sharp growth in mortgage loans, where loan volume increased to 60 billion crowns," Nordbanken said.
"The market share in this important segment rose to 12.1 percent, up 1.7 percentage points during the most recent 12 months."
Savings in mutual funds rose very sharply during the latter half of the first quarter and assets under management amounted to 97 billion crowns at the end of the quarter.
Loan losses fell to 110 million crowns from 280 million with the loan loss level decreasing to 0.2 percent from 0.3 percent.
-- Birgitta Forsberg, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1006 ($ = 7.804 Swedish Crowns)
